n: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, trusting its many chariots and strong cavalry, but who do not look to the Holy One of Israel or seek the Lord.
But God is wise too! He will bring disaster and will not take back His words. He will rise against the wicked and those who help them.

f.g: An ironic jab at Judah’s “wise” politicians.

n: The Egyptians are mere humans, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the Lord stretches out His hand, both helper and helped will fall together.

f.w: the Egyptians are men, and not God

n: Like a lion growling over its prey, unafraid of a crowd of shouting shepherds, the Lord of hosts will come down to fight for Mount Zion.
Like birds hovering over their nest, the Lord of hosts will shield Jerusalem; He will defend, deliver, “pass over,” and rescue it. The word recalls the first Passover.

f.g: Hebrew pasoaḥ — the same root as Passover (Exodus 12:13).

n: So return, people of Israel, to the One you have so deeply rebelled against.
In that day everyone will throw away the silver and gold idols their own sinful hands made.
Assyria will fall by a sword that is not human. No mortal soldier will defeat it — fulfilled when the angel of the Lord struck the Assyrian camp.

f.w: the sword, not of a mighty man

n: Assyria’s stronghold will crumble in terror and its officers flee in panic from the Lord’s banner. The Lord’s fire burns in Zion and His furnace is in Jerusalem — His presence protects His people and consumes His enemies.
